tools.name: save_memory
tools.description: Store a developer memory (fact, preference, decision, architecture detail). Memories persist across all Claude Code sessions and are available in future conversations.

memory_type.description: Type: identity, preference, architecture, decision, bug, dependency, pattern, context. Custom types also accepted for non-developer domains.

category.description: Category: frontend, backend, database, devops, testing, security, performance, tooling, api, general. Custom categories also accepted for non-developer domains.

scope.description: global = applies everywhere, project = specific to this codebase, team = shared with team members

team_id.description: Team ID (required when scope is "team"). The memory will be shared with all team members.

tags.description: Optional tags for grouping/threading memories (max 5 tags, each max 30 chars). E.g., ["marketing-campaign", "feb-2026"]

ttl.description: Set an expiration time. Use for temporary context like current task status. Format: "24h", "7d", "30d". Memory auto-archives after expiry.

project_id.description: Project identifier override (auto-detected from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or git remote if omitted)

tools.name: save_rule
tools.description: Save a mandatory rule that will ALWAYS be followed in every session. Rules bypass scoring and decay — they are injected into every conversation, every time. Use for absolute requirements like "NEVER do X" or "ALWAYS do Y".

content.description: The rule to enforce (e.g., "NEVER use -latest model aliases", "ALWAYS apply changes to both class-chat.php AND class-maas.php")

subject.description: Short label for the rule, e.g. "model_aliases", "companions_parity"

scope.description: global = applies to all projects, project = only this codebase

category.description: Category for organization: frontend, backend, security, general, etc.

project_id.description: Project identifier override (auto-detected from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or git remote if omitted)

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: List all mandatory rules for the current project and/or globally. Rules are always-on memories that surface in every session.

scope.description: Filter: all = project + global, project = this project only, global = global only

tools.name: delete_rule
tools.description: Delete a mandatory rule by its memory ID. Use list_rules to find the ID first.

memory_id.description: The memory ID of the rule to delete

tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Think Before You Speak. Call this BEFORE making any suggestion, recommendation, or action plan. Sends the topic to a fast keyword search and returns any relevant prior context — previous attempts, decisions, contacts, evaluations. This prevents suggesting things that were already tried, rejected, or completed. Fast and cheap — use liberally.

message.description: What you are about to suggest or respond about. Be specific — include names, topics, approaches.

tools.name: recall_memories
tools.description: Search stored memories using semantic search. Returns memories ranked by relevance, importance, and recency. Use this to find relevant context from past sessions.

category.description: Filter by category (e.g., "backend", "frontend", or any custom category)

importance_min.description: Only return memories with importance >= this value

team_id.description: Optional override. Team memories are automatically included for team/enterprise users.

context_type.description: Optional context type that shifts scoring weights. debugging = boost bug/pattern memories, planning = boost architecture/decision, reviewing = boost pattern/preference.

synthesize.description: When true and 3+ results are found, returns an AI-synthesized summary combining all memories into a coherent answer.

tools.name: extract_memories
tools.description: Extract memories from a conversation exchange using AI. Send the developer message and assistant response, and the server identifies facts worth remembering (architecture decisions, preferences, bug fixes, etc.).

tools.name: get_project_context
tools.description: Load top memories for the current project plus relevant global memories. Use at the start of a session to get full context from previous sessions. Optionally pass context to get memories most relevant to your current task.

project_id.description: Project identifier (auto-detected from git remote if omitted)

context.description: Optional context to improve relevance ranking (e.g., current task or topic)

context_type.description: Optional context type that shifts scoring weights. debugging = boost bug/pattern memories, planning = boost architecture/decision, reviewing = boost pattern/preference.

compact.description: When true (default), returns only formatted_context text instead of full JSON arrays. Saves ~60% tokens.

limit.description: Max total memories to return (default 25). Lower values save context tokens.

team_id.description: Optional override. Team memories are automatically included for team/enterprise users.

tools.name: list_memories
tools.description: List stored memories with optional filters by type, category, scope, or project.

category.description: Filter by category (e.g., "backend", "frontend", or any custom category)

importance_min.description: Only return memories with importance >= this value

untyped.description: When true, only return memories with no memory_type set

sort_by.description: Sort order: importance (default), updated, created, referenced (most used first), least_used

tools.name: delete_memory
tools.description: Delete a specific memory by its ID. This is permanent.

tools.name: update_memory
tools.description: Update an existing memory's content, importance, or scope.

category.description: New category (e.g., "backend", "frontend", or any custom category)

tools.name: bulk_delete
tools.description: Delete multiple memories at once by their IDs. Maximum 100 IDs per call. This is permanent.

ids.description: Array of memory IDs to delete (max 100)

tools.name: bulk_update
tools.description: Update multiple memories at once. Each item needs a memory_id and fields to update. Maximum 50 items per call.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Get current usage statistics — memory count, extractions this month, tier info, projects.

tools.name: export_memories
tools.description: Export all memories as JSON. Use this to back up memories or transfer them to another project.

tools.name: import_memories
tools.description: Bulk import memories from a JSON array. Each memory needs at minimum a content field. Deduplication is applied automatically.

memories.description: JSON string containing an array of memory objects. Each must have "content", optionally: memory_type, category, subject, importance, scope.

tools.name: ingest_document
tools.description: Extract memories from a document by splitting it into chunks and processing each one. Great for onboarding — feed in READMEs, architecture docs, or API specs to quickly build project context.

text.description: The document text to ingest (up to 50K characters)

document_type.description: Type hint for extraction (e.g., readme, api_docs, architecture, changelog)

tools.name: save_session_summary
tools.description: Save a summary of the current coding session. Captures what was accomplished, decisions made, and next steps. Stored as a session_summary memory for future reference.

summary.description: Summary of the session — what was done, key decisions, and next steps

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: List all tags in use across your memories, with counts. Use this to see what threads/groups exist and find related memories by tag.

tools.name: link_memories
tools.description: Connect two related memories with a named relationship. Use this to build a knowledge graph — e.g., linking a bug fix to the architecture decision that caused it, or connecting a preference to the pattern it led to.

related_memory_id.description: The target memory ID to link to

relationship.description: How the memories relate: led_to (A caused B), contradicts (A conflicts with B), extends (A builds on B), related (general connection)

tools.name: get_memory_links
tools.description: View all memories linked to a specific memory. Returns the relationship type and full memory details for each connection. Use this to explore the knowledge graph around a memory.

memory_id.description: The memory ID to get links for

tools.name: get_memory_versions
tools.description: View the edit history of a memory. Shows all previous versions with timestamps and what changed. Useful for understanding how a decision or fact evolved over time.

memory_id.description: The memory ID to get version history for

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Get a memory health dashboard with insights: most recalled memories, never-recalled memories, stale memories, growth trends, and breakdowns by type and category. Use this to identify cleanup opportunities and understand memory usage patterns.

project_id.description: Filter analytics to a specific project. Omit for current project. Use "all" for cross-project analytics.

tools.name: promote_memory
tools.description: Promote a project-scoped memory to global scope so it applies across all projects. Use this when you discover a preference or pattern that should be universal — e.g., "user prefers tabs over spaces" or "always use Bun instead of npm".

memory_id.description: The project memory ID to promote to global scope

tools.name: consolidate_memories
tools.description: Consolidate related memories into fewer, richer memories. Finds clusters of memories sharing the same subject (3+ memories required), then uses AI to synthesize each cluster into 1-2 comprehensive facts. Originals are archived (not deleted) with full version history. Use dry_run=true to preview without making changes. Great for cleaning up memory clutter after many sessions.

subject.description: Consolidate only memories with this exact subject (e.g., "auth_system"). Omit to auto-detect all qualifying clusters.

memory_type.description: Only consolidate memories of this type

category.description: Only consolidate memories in this category

dry_run.description: When true, preview consolidation results without making changes. Recommended for first use.

tools.name: save_task
tools.description: Create a task that persists across sessions. Tasks are tracked with status (pending, in_progress, done, blocked) and priority (high, medium, low). Use this to maintain continuity on multi-session work.

title.description: Short task title (e.g., "Fix auth bug in login flow")

description.description: Detailed description of what needs to be done

project_id.description: Project identifier override (auto-detected from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or git remote if omitted)

tools.name: get_tasks
tools.description: Get tasks for the current project. Returns tasks filtered by status — defaults to showing pending and in_progress tasks. Use at session start to pick up where you left off.

status.description: Filter by task status. "all" returns pending + in_progress + blocked (excludes done).

include_done.description: When true, also include completed tasks

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Update a task's status, title, description, or priority. Use this to mark tasks as in_progress, done, or blocked as you work.

tools.name: save_correction
tools.description: Save a correction pattern — what went wrong and what the right approach is. These are surfaced automatically when similar situations arise in future sessions, helping avoid repeated mistakes.

wrong_approach.description: What was done incorrectly (e.g., "Used npm install instead of bun add")

right_approach.description: The correct approach (e.g., "Always use bun add for this project")

context.description: When/where this applies (e.g., "package management in monorepo")

scope.description: global = applies everywhere, project = specific to this codebase

project_id.description: Project identifier override (auto-detected from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or git remote if omitted)

tools.name: set_reminder
tools.description: Set a reminder that surfaces automatically at the start of your next session. Use for follow-ups, things to check, or deferred work. Reminders auto-archive after being shown.

content.description: What to remind about (e.g., "Check if PR #42 was merged")

ttl.description: How long to keep the reminder alive. Format: "24h", "7d", "30d". Default: 7 days.

tools.name: get_stale_memories
tools.description: Find memories that may be outdated based on age and access patterns. Returns memories that haven't been recalled or updated recently, so you can review, update, or delete them.

days_threshold.description: Consider memories stale if not accessed in this many days (default: 30)

tools.name: get_file_changes
tools.description: Show what files changed since your last session. Compares the current git state to a snapshot saved when your previous session ended. Helps you understand what happened between sessions.

tools.name: feedback_memory
tools.description: Signal whether a recalled memory was useful or irrelevant. Helps improve future recall quality over time. Use after recalling memories to indicate which were helpful vs noise.

memory_id.description: The memory ID to give feedback on

signal.description: "useful" boosts the memory's ranking, "irrelevant" reduces its importance. For skills, "useful" boosts confidence, "irrelevant" reduces it.

tools.name: generate_skills
tools.description: Manually trigger skill generation from your corrections, preferences, and patterns. Skills are behavioral directives that auto-improve how the AI works with you. CogmemAi also generates skills automatically when enough evidence accumulates — this tool lets you trigger it manually or preview candidates.

subject.description: Generate skills for a specific subject. Omit to scan all subjects.

project_id.description: Project to generate skills for (auto-detected if omitted)

dry_run.description: When true, preview skill candidates without generating them

tools.name: extract_principles
tools.description: Analyze memory clusters and extract underlying factual principles or patterns. Principles are observations about your project — "this codebase tends to have X" — not behavioral instructions (those are skills). Use dry_run to preview candidates first.

subject.description: Focus on a specific subject area. Omit to scan all subjects.

project_id.description: Project to extract principles for (auto-detected if omitted)

dry_run.description: When true, preview principle candidates without generating them
